newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell stops Nigerian Bonny crude exports due strike.
newsitem.headline: Shell stops Nigerian Bonny crude exports due strike.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Tuesday it had declared force majeure on export of Bonny crude oil because of a strike by contractors that handle the berthing and loading of tankers.
"We have declared force majeure on Bonny exports with effect from yesterday," a Shell spokesman said in Lagos.

"This action was taken in response to a strike by workers of a contractor that operates support services for tankers berthing and loading at Bonny terminal." Shell's Bonny output is about half of the roughly 950,000 barrels per day (bpd) it produces in Nigeria.
The spokesman said the force majeure would hold for as long as the strike by the staff of the oil services company known as O.I.L. lasted.
Bonny crude oil is produced and exported in the eastern division of Shell's operation in Nigeria.
The company spokesman denied reports in Nigerian newspapers on Tuesday that communal conflicts in the western division had forced Shell to cut output there by 15 percent.
